facts.fact: The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies says mobile banking data transits infrastructure Sudan neither owns nor regulates, with no statutory requirement governing data localization or cross-border transfer; it only proposes localisation as a first legislative tranche.

note: Fact dated to the document's published date, as it gives no other date for the absence.

facts.fact: Global Voices states Sudan has no law imposing data localization; it reports a former senior Central Bank official saying the Bank and other government bodies work under an undeclared localization policy, while DNS lookups showed several government websites hosted abroad. Dated to the article's published date.

systems.system: Undeclared data localization policy of the Central Bank and other government institutions

note: Document states nothing on this for the country.
The author argues for a law and authority to impose localisation; no rule is stated as drafted or in force, and central bank internal requirements are not described.

facts.fact: The article says banking activity in Sudan runs on foreign-hosted apps without any legal requirement governing data localisation or cross-border transfer.
